rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (kp 8.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.0), 60 trials with zero finishes. Progress rose from 0.04-0.125 to 0.18 on the oval, 0.10 on the s-bend and 0.085 on the slalom, and score rose from 27.4 to 49.8, so the proportional gain is the right lever. Two signs point to overshoot rather than a stable fix. steering_oscillation rose from about 0.07 to 0.13-0.15 on all tracks, and the oval reached 0.1517, just above the 0.15 threshold in the Evaluator's plan. max_error did not fall; it went from 0.060 to 0.066 on the oval, so the robot still leaves the 0.06 m band. The s-bend score spread (19.5 to 57.2) shows the run is sensitive to seed. Action: reduce kp from 8.0 to 6.0, the step the Evaluator named, and keep kd at 0.2 to damp the response. Geometry, base_speed, ki and line_loss are unchanged, so this race isolates the gain change. Expected result: steering_oscillation falls back to about 0.10, max_error stays near 0.06 or below, and progress holds at or above the kp 8 level (about 0.15 to 0.2 on the oval). Hypotheses: (1) if oscillation drops and progress keeps rising, the gain is near the stable range and sensor geometry is next. (2) if progress still stalls at one point with low oscillation, the 25 mm tape and 12 mm sensors leave a dead band near centre, so the next revision should set sensor_size 0.016 and keep kp 6.0. (3) if the robot tracks the line but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6. Measurements to see next: progress and max_error per track, steering_oscillation, and line_loss_events, to show whether the offset is gone or the robot is still leaving the line.
